 This Petition Is Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner being the sole accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in Crime No.182/2022 of Honnali Police Station, pending on the file of the learned Principal Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC, Honnali, Davanagere District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323, 302 and 316 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Jayabai.
2. Heard Sri.Harsha G., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC:21300 "Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of bail.
The mother of the deceased lodged the first information against the petitioner regarding commission of the offences as stated above.
The petitioner had married the deceased on 09.06.2020 and the incident had occurred on 07.09.2022 i.e., within a period of two years.
It is stated that as per post mortem report, the deceased had sustained grievous injuries, which are anti mortem in nature.
Even though the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is a case of accident, the dead body was subjected to post mortem examination when it was at the stage of decomposition.
There is no explanation as to why the petitioner has not filed any complaint after the so called accident and why the deceased was not taken immediately to the hospital.
The allegations made are NC: 2024:KHC:21300 very serious in nature.
Charge sheet is already filed which prima facie discloses the commission of the offences under Section 498A and 302 IPC.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.

SD/-
